list.snippet: I44: This is the ICD-10 code for atrioventricular block.
.0: This specific code indicates first-degree AV block.

text_blocks.snippet: First-degree AV block refers to a condition where the electrical impulses from the atria (upper chambers of the heart) take longer than usual to reach the ventricles (lower chambers of the heart). This is typically detected on an electrocardiogram (ECG) as a prolonged PR interval (the time interval between the onset of the P wave, representing atrial depolarization, and the onset of the QRS complex, representing ventricular depolarization).
